title: Apple GPU prefill shared-staging BK sensitivity
question: With BM=8, BN=16, and one thread per output held fixed, how does BK=16, 32, 64, or 128 change rotating packed-QKV prefill timing?
hypotheses: Smaller BK uses less threadgroup storage but executes more K phases, barriers, and loop-control work.
Larger BK executes fewer phases and barriers but uses more threadgroup storage and lengthens each cooperative-load and shared-arithmetic phase.
At least one non-32 BK may materially improve the large-M rotating workloads enough to justify a later comparison against the direct no-staging control.
unchanged: BF16 input, weight, bias, and output with FP32 accumulation and one final BF16 cast
row-major X[M,K], W[N,K], and Y[M,N] layouts
128 threads per threadgroup and one scalar output per thread
cooperative X and W staging with zero fill at M, N, and K tails
two uniform threadgroup barriers per K phase
one enqueue per layer and one completion boundary per measured workload
no weight packing, quantization, or public dispatch change

correctness.authority: tests/test_linear.mojo plus each benchmark variant's untimed exact-unit-output gate
required_cases: Existing BK=32 oracle, exact-tile, ragged-tail, and Qwen-width cases
M=9 K=129 N=17 host-reference comparison for BK=16, 32, 64, and 128
Existing decode, packed-QKV, direct-control, and rowwise tests remain passing
correctness.edge_rationale: K=129 requires a partial final K phase for every BK and M=9, N=17 require partial output tiles.

workload_matrix.weights: 24 distinct allocations rotated once per measured workload iteration

measurement_protocol.decisive_command: uv run --locked python benchmarks/run_linear_prefill_bk_sweep.py --blocks 4 --experiment-id EXP-0009 --run-id EXP-0009-RUN-001 --recorded --output-dir <absolute-external-path>/EXP-0009-RUN-001
measurement_protocol.order_balance: Each BK occupies each of the four within-workload execution positions exactly once.
measurement_protocol.paired_statistic: Within each block and M, candidate median divided by BK=32 median; summarize the four ratios with their median and retain every ratio.
measurement_protocol.environment: Clean immutable commit, AC power, no reported thermal or performance warning, Apple GPU plus Metal runtime identity, and MODULAR_DEBUG unset.

classification_rule.material_improvement: Median paired ratio <= 0.95 and candidate faster in at least three of four blocks.
classification_rule.material_regression: Median paired ratio >= 1.05 and candidate slower in at least three of four blocks.

advance_rule.required: A non-32 BK must materially improve M=64, 128, and 256 against BK=32 and must not materially regress any tested M>=8.
advance_rule.tie_break: If multiple BKs qualify, advance the one with the lowest median of its M=64, 128, and 256 paired ratios.
advance_rule.next_step: Compare the qualifying BK against the direct 8x16 no-staging control under a separately frozen protocol.
advance_rule.production_decision: None. This sensitivity screen cannot select a public dispatch path.

nonclaims: BK is not the only generated-code difference: changing it also changes loop trip counts, cooperative-load work per phase, and shared-arithmetic loop length.
Source-requested operand traffic is equal across these four variants at K=896, but no hardware cache, fabric, or DRAM traffic is measured.
Timing cannot separately identify barrier, shared-memory, occupancy, instruction, compiler, or cache costs.
A winner against BK=32 is not proven faster than the direct control or the public rowwise path.
No end-to-end prompt, model, or decoder throughput result.
